text: Suspect, in general, those who remarkably affect any one virtue; who raise it above all others, and who, in a manner, intimate that they possess it exclusively. I say suspect them, for they are commonly impostors; but do not be sure that they are always so; for I have sometimes known saints really religious, blusterers really brave, reformers of manners really honest, and prudes really chaste.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XCVII, to his son, London, December 19, Old Style 1749
